newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-DUNN WINS MEN'S 200 MEDLEY WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-DUNN WINS MEN'S 200 MEDLEY WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Australia's Matthew Dunn completed his second successive golden individual medley double at the world short-course championships when he retained his title in the 200 event on Sunday.
Dunn, who retained his 400 individual medley crown on Thursday and won a relay gold on Friday, trailed seventh on the butterfly leg in which 30-year-old American Ron Karnaugh set the pace.

But the Australian pulled up to second behind Britain's James Hickman at the end of the backstroke leg, took the lead on the breaststroke and retained it through the concluding freestyle, winning in one minute 57.46 seconds.
Germany's Christian Keller, winner of the event at the first edition of the championships in 1993, took the silver in 1:58.35.
Karnaugh, joint bronze medallist with Keller in Thursday's 400 individual medley final, emerged with another bronze in 1:59.12 ahead of 200 butterfly gold medallist Hickman (1:59.49).
